question: Effective origin-change allowlist threshold (bins per monthly analysis window) per year
summary: A retrospective allowlist removes (prefix, new origin) pairs that change in at least T five-minute bins of their calendar month: T = 50 in 2024, the year of the recall validation, and T = round(50 x days / 7), i.e. 50 bins per week or 200-221 bins per month, in 2022, 2023, 2025 and 2026, so the 2024 allowlist is about four times stricter.

validation_threshold_note.text: The 2024 recall validation (10-49 peers: 0.662-0.727) scored the flat T = 50 event tables. The other years' event tables used T = 200-221. Their own same-run windowed evaluations at 10-49 peers 2023: 0.78-0.86 over 9 months; 2026: 0.81-0.88 over 8 months (none for 2022 and 2025, which had no Cloudflare hijack labels when they ran). These figures are not a controlled comparison: label coverage and year differ.

leak_events: The leak identifier (first-seen path triples: leakcheck.triple_candidates/classify_triples, leak_events.build_events) applies no allowlist; see code_and_docs.leak_* citations.
method: Effective threshold T bounded from the outputs: max over kept pairs of sum(n_bins) < T <= min(bins) of flapper_whitelist.parquet; summary.json records only the unscaled flapper_bins.

No 2024 month was re-run after 86b9b4b2.
